long_biography.plain_text:
Scotch & Soda was a small Dutch menswear label before Eric Pieter Bijlsma, Joep Krouwels and Patrick Munsters acquired most of the company in 2000. They relaunched it, refreshed the brand and widened its reach through thousands of wholesale outlets and a growing network of owned shops. New lines extended the business into women's clothing, children's wear and denim.

The partners sold the company to Kellwood and Sun Capital in 2011, while its management initially remained in place. Bijlsma later joined Oakley Capital's North Sails apparel transaction as a partner, major shareholder and chief executive. The role united his experience in brand development with a long personal interest in sailing. He subsequently backed another apparel venture built around reworking existing garments, extending a career defined by acquiring, repositioning and investing in fashion brands.

uncertainties.detail: Scotch & Soda was founded by Laurens Hompes in 1985. Bijlsma, Krouwels and Munsters acquired most of the existing business around 2000 and relaunched it. Some later articles call the trio founders because they created the modern brand, but this dossier uses acquirer, co-owner and operator to preserve the legal and historical chronology.

Contemporary Dutch reports identify Bijlsma within the co-owner and management trio, and later FashionUnited coverage explicitly calls him the former chief executive. The known-for title therefore combines co-owner and CEO rather than assigning the general-manager title reported for Joep Krouwels or Patrick Munsters' creative-director role.

The owner record, yacht sources, FashionUnited and Textilia generally use Eric. One RetailTrends article uses Erik, apparently as a spelling variation or editorial error. Eric is retained because it dominates the identity-matched record and aligns with the full corporate name Eric Pieter Bijlsma.

Corporate-record aggregations connect Eric Pieter Bijlsma to Scotch & Soda entities, supporting Pieter at high confidence. No accessible first-party personal biography or civil record was located, so confidence remains below very high.

The documented fortune arose from an acquired brand that Bijlsma and his partners operationally transformed and sold. Public sources do not explain his earlier career, family resources or the acquisition financing, so Self-made is used without the independent-start or advantaged-start subtype.

Bijlsma's later North Sails Apparel shareholder-chief-executive role and investment in another fashion venture show continued sector activity, but no authoritative current biography identifies a single present principal company. Fashion & Retail remains the primary industry, while the known-for title uses the better-documented Scotch & Soda role.

LinkedIn search returns at least four Eric Bijlsma profiles, including unrelated technology, insurance and sporting-goods professionals. No personal profile was collision-safe through Scotch & Soda, North Sails or another direct anchor, and no verified Instagram or personal website was found; no social is proposed.

The official acquisition announcement said financial terms were undisclosed, while later publications give materially different reported values. Neither biography uses a transaction amount or converts a company-level figure into Bijlsma's personal proceeds or current net worth.

Apparel retail is the minimum useful active tag because Scotch & Soda's wholesale and owned-store expansion was the defining wealth mechanism. Apparel manufacturing, sailing, sportswear and circular fashion are meaningful context but do not warrant overlapping owner-level tags on the current evidence.
Gio, Firefly and competitive-sailing records are used only to resolve identity. The biographies contain no vessel name, ownership claim, race result, specification or leisure detail.

review.notes:
Terminal resolved-person dossier. Identity confidence is 99 through the Gio-to-Firefly vessel continuity, official race-owner records and fashion-industry reporting that independently identifies the same Dutch competitive sailor as the former Scotch & Soda and later North Sails Apparel executive. Wealth is classified Fashion & Retail, Fashion & Retail, Self-made and Operator. Operator deliberately preserves the fact that Bijlsma acquired and relaunched an existing 1985 label rather than founding the original company. Pieter, a known-for title, male gender and biography are proposed; no collision-safe personal social is proposed. No shared source, progress file, compiled artifact or live system was changed.

Owner-tag consolidation research context: [1] Apparel retail: Bijlsma's defining wealth mechanism was the relaunch and international expansion of Scotch & Soda through wholesale distribution, owned shops and multiple apparel lines; the active tag is assigned. [2] Apparel manufacturing: The sources reviewed focus on branding, wholesale and retail rather than a separately defining manufacturing platform, so this overlapping tag is omitted. [3] Sailing and North Sails: Personal competitive sailing helps resolve identity and shaped a later apparel role, but the underlying wealth-producing activity remains fashion-brand ownership and operation. [4] Circular fashion: A later investment supports current sector continuity but is not documented at sufficient scale for an additional owner-level tag.
